messages.text: Standup {short_date}. {prs} PRs open, oldest review is {age} hours. Focus today is {focus}.
Good. Keep two review slots free until noon, that is what the rotation in the deploy runbook assumes.
Done, the board reflects it.

Tell the channel the truth and give a real choice: wait for green, split the PR, or land behind a flag. No vague reruns.
Noted for the support handover, I will fold the wording into the macros this week.
Standup {short_date}. Two overnight pages, both on {service}, both resolved by the runbook steps. Nothing outstanding this morning.
Third alert was a disk threshold at {time}. The dashboard had the growth curve, which is exactly why we track it.
Good. That is the runbook working, not luck.
Standup {short_date}. One reviewer is out sick, the {focus} queue is being redistributed. {prs} PRs affected.
I can absorb four this afternoon. Move the small fixes rather than the schema changes.
Agreed, reassigning now.
Standup {short_date}. Reminder on migrations: every schema change ships with a down path. The deploy gate cannot check intent and that is how a stuck rollback happens.
I will spot check the last {prs} merges today and come back with numbers.
Same request from QA for release notes on the build, {prs} builds last week came in without any.
Standup {short_date}. Review queue is {prs} deep, nothing older than two days. Rotation is on top of it.
Fine. A hotfix never waits in the queue, we settle the paperwork afterwards.
Two new joiners shadow the standup today, they will be watching {suite} runs.
Standup {short_date}. One near miss yesterday: a config change almost shipped to cloud and self-hosted at once, caught at the second approval. Reported the same day, exactly right.
We will add a paired review step to the deploy checklist rather than blame anyone.
That is the fix. System, not person.
Standup {short_date}. Quiet morning, {prs} PRs open, oldest {age} hours. The {service} team has spare review capacity if anyone needs to offload.
QA is clear too, all urgent regressions from yesterday closed before {time}.
Then use the slack to catch up on the outstanding docs updates.
Standup {short_date}. Load test scheduled for {time} against staging {service}. Announce it in the channel first, not after the graphs spike.
Thank you. An alert is not an alert if on-call cannot tell it from a drill.
Support knows, the status page stays untouched for staging runs.
Standup {short_date}. {focus} follow-ups are drifting past six weeks in the backlog. That is a quality issue before it is a planning one.
I will pull the list today and we can triage by risk rather than by date filed.
Yes. Bring the numbers to the leads sync.
Nightly {short_date}: {pipeline} green on all suites, {tests} tests in {minutes} minutes. Backup of {target} completed and verified.
Artifact registry is up, no builds stuck in the upload queue.
Nightly {short_date}: the {suite} suite failed twice on {pipeline}. Merges to that area are blocked until it clears. Everything else is green.
Understood. If it holds past midday, tell the channel so nobody is waiting on a build that is not coming.
Nightly {short_date}: all green. Median pipeline time yesterday {minutes} minutes from push to verdict, {tests} tests total.
That is the number I want on the release review slide, not the average.
Nightly {short_date}: rerun on {pipeline} after a runner image update, green on the second pass. Documented as a non-conformity with the image tag.
Tag is pinned in the registry, and the base image issue is reported upstream.
Nightly {short_date}: green. Two flaky cases quarantined in the {suite} suite, both timing sensitive, both ticketed with traces attached.
Seen. That was the {time} runner batch, we will move those cases off the shared pool.
Nightly {short_date}: green. One critical alert on {target} paged within 30 seconds and was acknowledged, logged with who took it.
Good. A critical page is never delivered only by email.
Nightly {short_date}: green. Backup of {target} completed with the checksum verified, report attached to the daily record.
The standby replica is caught up if the primary starts lagging again.
Nightly {short_date}: green. {tests} tests, {minutes} minute median. e2e-nightly is the constraint, the two hour window leaves no room for a slow runner.
Understood, mobile-build moves to the early slot from now on.
Weekly infra summary, week ending {short_date}: {flaky} flaky tests quarantined, uptime {uptime}, alert backlog {backlog}.
Flaky tests are the number I care about most. Which suites and which cause?
Mostly timing in the calls suite, one real race in files. All ticketed with traces the same day.
Weekly infra summary, week ending {short_date}: {flaky} quarantined, uptime {uptime}. Pipeline time held inside target on every branch except mobile.
Mobile is not urgent, but people still wait on it. Can we split the build into two shards instead of one?
Yes, from next week. That cuts the worst case by twelve minutes.
Weekly infra summary, week ending {short_date}: {flaky} quarantined, uptime {uptime}, backlog {backlog}. One runner pool is close to end of life and drains first.
Procurement has the replacement hosts ordered, delivery is expected before the old pool retires.
Good. Losing the pool mid week would stall every merge.
Device lab {short_date}: build {build} on {devices} devices, all passed. Blocked tickets: {blocked}.
Confirmed in the run log, results attached to the release ticket before lunch.
Device lab {short_date}: build {build}, {devices} passed, two failed on the older Androids. Both failures ticketed with screen recordings.
Both loaded first for tomorrow, fixes are already in review.
Device lab {short_date}: build {build} landed after the run started. Held for tomorrow morning per the runbook, nobody chases results today.
Correct call. Better a day later than a run nobody can trust.
Device lab {short_date}: {devices} devices through build {build}. Waiting list for the loaner phones is long again, regression day always is.
The second regression day is worth costing out. Bring it to the leads sync with the booking numbers.
Device lab {short_date}: courier took two test phones to Sofia this morning for the calls work. Back Thursday, the rack holds {devices} until then.
Nothing blocked this time, but log the loan in the device register. Below ten devices and we lose the full matrix.
Device lab {short_date}: build {build}, {devices} passed, blocked tickets {blocked}. Trakia Training Room is booked for the community webinar this evening as usual.
Forty two registered for the onboarding session, that is the best turnout so far.

Support desk {short_date}: {resolved} resolved, {breaches} breaches. Two orgs asked for workspace exports today, both sent to the DPO mailbox rather than handled from the ticket.
Exactly right. The requester gets verified as the org owner before anything is released, and admins asking for member content do not count.
Support desk {short_date}: {resolved} resolved, {new} new. One customer upset about an invoice, itemised copy sent by email and the tone kept neutral.
Good. Billing is neutral and itemised, never defensive.
Support desk {short_date}: {resolved} resolved, {issue}. The desk coped, but we are one person short on Fridays.
I will look at the Friday rotation this week. That is the day new tickets spike.
Support desk {short_date}: {resolved} resolved, {breaches} breaches, {new} new. Two onboarding calls, one booked in advance and one on the spot.
The on the spot one is the problem. Offer the call in the welcome email every time.
Support desk {short_date}: {resolved} resolved. Queue was empty by 18:00, and {issue}.
Thanks, I will keep an eye on the status page delay. If it lags again we fix the pipeline rather than post manually a third time.

People search when they are stuck. Every point of clarity there is worth two elsewhere.

No data loss, only confusing. Confirmed against two support tickets before deciding.
Standup notes {short_date}: {area} work continues, {metric}. Blocked on nothing.
Staging matches production config now, so the surprise we had last month should not repeat.
Good. That surprise cost us a day.
Accessibility pass on {area} finished {short_date}. Contrast tokens are enforced in the shared components now, not per screen.

Can we get the same treatment on the email templates?
